content: Chapter Checklist This document serves as a comprehensive guide for structuring chapters and microchapters. For reference, the chapter on pericarditis can be used as an example to understand the process of creating and organizing chapters and microchapters effectively. Microchapter Guidelines Each microchapter should begin with the same page name. For instance, examples include Pericarditis overview, Pericarditis pathophysiology, and Pericarditis treatment. Only the first word of each chapter title should be capitalized. All microchapters listed in the template on the right-hand side must be included on the homepage of the main chapter. Each microchapter should incorporate the template provided on the right-hand side. It is not mandatory to create a microchapter for every title listed in the template. Irrelevant chapter titles can be removed from the microchapter template as needed. In some cases, there may be no primary or secondary prevention strategies. For example, there is no primary prevention strategy for pericarditis. Patient Information Page Conduct a thorough search of the National Library of Medicine and other government websites to ensure the patient information page is complete. The goal of this page is to provide a consumer-oriented overview that addresses the background, diagnosis, and treatment of the condition. The content should be written at an 8th-grade reading level to ensure accessibility and should avoid overly technical language. The page should include the following content: What is the condition? What are the symptoms of the condition? What causes the condition? Who is at the highest risk? When to seek urgent medical care. Treatment options. Where to find medical care for the condition. What to expect (outlook/prognosis). Possible complications. Sources of information. Remember to include a link to the WikiDoc page at the top of the patient information page. Overview The goal of the overview section is to provide a concise description of the key aspects of the condition, focusing on the background, diagnosis, and treatment. This text will appear in all Google searches and must be carefully crafted to ensure grammatical accuracy and clarity. The content should include: Background information. Etiology. A general summary of diagnosis and treatment. Where necessary, links to additional, more detailed microchapters should be provided. Pathophysiology The objective of this section is to explain the biological mechanisms underlying the disease state. The content should include: A description of embryological or developmental abnormalities. Molecular abnormalities. Genetic abnormalities. Pathogenesis. Pathology images. Efforts should be made to search for copyleft images of pathology specimens and videos on platforms such as YouTube. Additionally, resources like the Pathology Wiki and Ask Dr. Wiki should be consulted for relevant images.
